about.title: About - Corvid
about.updateAvailableTooltip: A newer version (v{{version}}) is available on GitHub. Click to view the release.
about.body: Corvid is a self-hostable, on-demand analysis platform designed for security specialists. It consolidates various security tools into a single, easy-to-use environment, streamlining everyday investigative tasks. Optimized for single-user operation, Corvid runs locally in a Docker container and is not intended for long-term data storage or management. Instead, it focuses on accelerating daily workflows, such as news aggregation and analysis, IOC and email investigations, and the creation of threat detection rules. To further enhance efficiency, Corvid integrates generative AI capabilities, providing additional support for analysis and decision-making. Beyond its practical applications, the project also serves as a personal playground for experimenting with new technologies and automation possibilities, potentially laying the foundation for a future commercial cloud platform.
about.nameNote: The name Corvid may still change in the future.

accessToken.title: Access Token
accessToken.description: The token this browser uses to authenticate with the backend. Copy it to unlock the app in another browser, or forget it to lock this one.
accessToken.forgetConfirm: This will sign you out of this browser. You'll need the token again (from the server logs, data/.access_token, or another already-unlocked browser) to get back in. Continue?
accessToken.regenerateConfirmBody: This immediately invalidates the current token. Every other browser tab, device, and the browser extension will need the new token entered manually before they work again. This browser updates automatically.
accessToken.regenerateSuccess: Token regenerated. Copy it now and update any other browser, device, or the browser extension.
accessToken.regenerateError: Failed to regenerate the access token.
accessToken.regenerateFixedByEnv: The access token is fixed via the API_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable and can't be regenerated here - unset it to allow regeneration.

backup.title: Backup & Restore
backup.description: Download a full backup of the database (all settings and history) plus the encryption key needed to decrypt stored API keys, or restore from a previously downloaded backup.
backup.unsupported: Backup/restore only supports the SQLite database backend (this deployment runs {{dialect}}). Use your database's own dump/restore tooling instead.

export.title: Download a backup
export.description: Includes the database and the encryption key. The access token is left out by default.
export.includeAccessToken: Include the access token (so a restore reproduces the exact same token)
export.passphraseHelper: If set, the archive is encrypted and this passphrase is required to restore it. There's no way to recover it if lost.

restore.title: Restore from a backup
restore.description: Overwrites the current database, encryption key, and (if included) access token. Takes effect only after the backend is restarted.
restore.warning: This replaces all current settings and history. It cannot be undone, and you must restart the backend afterwards for the restored data to take effect.
restore.confirmBody: This will overwrite the current database, encryption key, and (if included) access token. This cannot be undone. Type RESTORE to confirm.
restore.success: Restore complete. Restart the backend for the restored data to take effect.
restore.successWithToken: Restore complete. The access token was also restored - restart the backend, then enter the restored token if the app asks you to re-authenticate.

commands.title: Bot commands
commands.description: Let the bot act on messages you send it: /lookup <value> for a quick IOC lookup, /digest for recent unread alerts, /help for the command list. Off by default - a different trust boundary than outbound notifications, since the bot now acts on messages sent to it.
